Which loft repaired the greatest number of nets?
MATH_M2E.check: 51 is the greatest of the four counts, and it belongs to Kingsdown.

MATH_M2E.stem: A sailmaker counted the cringles worked into each of seven covers and recorded 6, 9, 4, 9, 7, 9, and 5. What is the mode of these seven counts?
MATH_M2E.check: 9 appears three times, more often than any other count.

MATH_M2E.stem: A sailmaker's case holds 8 steel needles and 12 bone needles and no others. One needle is taken from the case at random. What is the probability that the needle taken is bone?
MATH_M2E.check: There are 20 needles in all and 12 of them are bone, so 12/20 = 3/5.

MATH_M2E.stem: A triangular storm sail has sides measuring 13 feet, 14 feet, and 15 feet. What is the perimeter, in feet, of the sail?
A tarpaulin is cut as a trapezoid whose two parallel edges measure 10 feet and 14 feet and whose height is 6 feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the tarpaulin?
Two straight ropes cross each other at a single point, forming four angles. One of those four angles measures 118°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle vertically opposite it?
MATH_M2E.check: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the angle measures 118 degrees.

MATH_M2E.stem: A right triangular sail has legs of length 8 feet and 15 feet and a hypotenuse of length 17 feet. What is the sine of the angle opposite the 8-foot leg?
MATH_M2E.check: Sine is the opposite leg over the hypotenuse, which is 8/17.

MATH_M2H.stem: One rope in a sail loft is 3 times as long as a second rope. When 8 feet is cut from each of the two ropes, the piece left from the first is 5 times as long as the piece left from the second. How many feet long was the first rope before the cutting?
MATH_M2H.check: 3s - 8 = 5(s - 8) gives 2s = 32 and s = 16, so the first rope was 48 feet.

MATH_M2H.stem: In a sail loft's cutting plan, a straight edge passes through the points (-2, 11) and (6, -5) . Which of the following points also lies on that edge?
MATH_M2H.check: The slope is -16/8 = -2 and the line is y = -2x + 7, which gives y = -13 at x = 10.

MATH_M2H.stem: In the inequality \(px-8\le 3x+12\), p is a constant, and the solution to the inequality is \(x\ge-4\). What is the value of p ?
MATH_M2H.check: (p-3)x <= 20; reversing the inequality needs p - 3 < 0, and 20/(p-3) = -4 gives p - 3 = -5, so p = -2.

MATH_M2H.stem: Three lengths of rope are to be spliced together. Taken two at a time, the first and second measure 34 feet in all, the second and third measure 47 feet in all, and the first and third measure 39 feet in all. What is the length, in feet, of the third rope?
MATH_M2H.check: Adding all three pairs gives twice the total, so the total is 60 and the third is 60 - 34 = 26.

MATH_M2H.stem: A sail loft's charge C, in dollars, for a sail of area A square feet is a linear function of A. A sail of 120 square feet is charged $510 and a sail of 200 square feet is charged $750. Which equation gives C in terms of A ?
MATH_M2H.check: $240 more for 80 more square feet is $3 each, and 510 - 360 = 150.

MATH_M2H.stem: A finished canvas panel is accepted only if its width w, in inches, satisfies \(\lvert w-34.5\rvert\le 0.8\). What is the least width, in inches, that is accepted?
MATH_M2H.check: The width lies between 34.5 - 0.8 and 34.5 + 0.8, so the least accepted width is 33.7.

MATH_M2H.stem:
In the system of equations below, k is a constant.
4x + 3y = k
x - y = 2
The solution to the system has y = 6. What is the value of k ?
The functions f and g satisfy f(x) = 2x + 7 and f(g(x)) = 6x - 1 for every value of x. Which expression gives g(x) ?
MATH_M2H.check: 2g(x) + 7 = 6x - 1 gives 2g(x) = 6x - 8 and g(x) = 3x - 4.

MATH_M2H.stem: For a two-part tackle, the combined stretch k of the falls is related to the individual stretches p and q by \(\frac{1}{k}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}\), where p, q and k are all positive. Which expression gives k in terms of p and q ?
MATH_M2H.check: 1/k = (q+p)/(pq), so k = pq/(p+q).

MATH_M2H.stem: A rectangular panel of canvas has an area of 96 square feet and a perimeter of 44 feet. What is the length, in feet, of its longer side?
MATH_M2H.check: Length plus width is 22 and their product is 96, so the sides are 16 and 6.

MATH_M2H.stem: For a > 0, which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{50a^{7}}\)?
MATH_M2H.check: 50a^7 = 25 a^6 times 2a, and the square root of that is 5 a^3 root(2a).

MATH_M2H.stem: The function f is defined by \(f(x)=x^{2}-14x+53\). The least value of f occurs at x = a, and that least value is b. What is the value of a + b ?
MATH_M2H.check: The vertex is at x = 7 and f(7) = 49 - 98 + 53 = 4, so a + b = 11.

MATH_M2H.stem: The expression \(x^{2}-10x+k\), where k is a constant, can be written in the form \((x-5)^{2}-9\). What is the value of k ?
A sail loft blends its canvas yarn from 3 parts flax costing $2.40 a pound and 2 parts cotton costing $1.65 a pound, by weight. What is the cost, in dollars, of one pound of the blend?

Two seamers working together, each at a constant rate, finish a suit of canvas in 12 hours. Working alone at that same constant rate, the first seamer would finish it in 20 hours. Working alone, how many hours would the second seamer take to finish it?
MATH_M2H.check: 1/12 - 1/20 = 1/30, so the second seamer alone takes 30 hours.

MATH_M2H.check: 43 sails were returned and 27 of them came from Westgate, so the probability is 27/43.

MATH_M2H.stem: The number of days needed to rig a set of shrouds varies inversely with the number of riggers put on the work. Six riggers would finish the work in 15 days. How many riggers are needed to finish the same work in 9 days?
MATH_M2H.check: 6(15) = 90 rigger-days, and 90/9 = 10 riggers.

MATH_M2H.stem: A length of canvas hose is a right circular cylinder with inner radius r and length L. A second length of canvas hose is a right circular cylinder with inner radius 2r and length \(\frac{L}{3}\). The volume enclosed by the second hose is how many times the volume enclosed by the first?
MATH_M2H.check: The volume scales by 2^2 for the radius and by 1/3 for the length, giving 4/3.

MATH_M2H.stem: A four-sided canvas cover is cut so that the measures of its four angles are in the ratio 2 to 3 to 4 to 6. What is the measure, in degrees, of its largest angle?
MATH_M2H.check: The four angles total 360 degrees over 15 equal parts, so one part is 24 and the largest is 6(24) = 144.

MATH_M2H.stem: A straight stay makes an acute angle \(\theta\) with level ground, and \(\tan\theta=\frac{7}{24}\). What is the value of \(\sin\theta\)?
MATH_M2H.check: A 7-24-25 right triangle gives a hypotenuse of 25, so the sine is 7/25.

MATH_M2H.stem: A triangular sail has a base of 18 feet and a height of 24 feet. A second triangular sail is similar to the first, and its base is 27 feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the second sail?
MATH_M2H.check: The first sail has area 216, the scale factor is 1.5, and 216(1.5)^2 = 486.
